key_insight: AutoDrude learns polarizable Drude force fields end-to-end from DFT data, enabling accurate polymer-electrolyte ion transport predictions without empirical charge scaling.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical, near-fixed-charge-cost route to simulate solid polymer electrolytes while capturing polarization-driven conductivity and transference trends more faithfully.
method: Differentiable parametrization of Drude force fields from DFT energies, forces, and dipoles
Hard-constraint and soft-constraint variants for fitting polarization behavior
Benchmarking against fixed-charge and charge-scaled models on PEO-LiTFSI transport properties
evidence_signal: On PEO-LiTFSI, the hard-constraint model matched experimental ionic conductivity with 17% MAPE, comparable to the best charge-scaled model at 16%, while also reproducing cation transference trends and low-concentration ion-pair behavior.
watch_item: The soft-constraint variant fit DFT reference data more closely but severely underpredicted conductivity, so good training loss alone does not guarantee reliable transport predictions.
paper_title: Drude, Where's My Charge? End-to-End Learning of Polarizable Drude Force Fields for Polymer Electrolytes
